transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, I keep hearing people talking about me. 

It happens a lot at work. I'll hear them through the conference room walls, or even coming from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's usually the board members or my staff, and they're saying that I'm ruining the company. It sounds so incredibly clear that I actually answer them back out loud... and it's only after I respond that I realize no one else in the room heard anything.
How long have you been hearing these voices or sounds — did this start recently, or has it been going on for weeks or months?
It's been going on for about three months now. The voices coming through the walls and from my phone... yeah, I'd say it's been happening for the past three months.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or other recreational drugs during these past three months?
No, I haven't. I don't use any drugs... no marijuana or stimulants, nothing like that. And I haven't been drinking alcohol either. I just don't use any of those things.

During these past three months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling extremely sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things, or on the other end, feeling unusually energetic, euphoric, or needing very little sleep?

No, I haven't noticed any changes like that. I mean, I'm not extremely sad or hopeless, and I certainly haven't lost interest in my company. And on the other end... no, I'm not unusually energetic either. I'm sleeping my normal amount. 

My mood is really just... normal, I guess. It's just those voices that are the issue.

Besides these voices, have you noticed any changes in how you think or speak—like trouble organizing your thoughts, or others telling you your speech is hard to follow—or a drop in your motivation, self-care, or ability to function at work?

Yeah, there has definitely been a drop in my motivation and how I'm functioning at the company. I mean, I used to be the person driving every single idea, always calling people right after openings and staying on top of everything. 

But now... I don't know, I can just sit at my desk for hours, just staring at the agenda without doing anything. I don't really talk much either—I barely speak to my husband or my staff these days. It's just... I feel almost nothing about the work I used to love so much. Everything just feels blank.

latest_inference.note: The presence of persistent auditory hallucinations (third-person, commenting) for 3 months, absence of mood episode or substance use, and now clear negative symptoms (avolition, alogia, affective flattening) with functional decline meet ICD-10 criteria for schizophrenia. This duration and symptom profile exceed the brief psychotic disorder (F23) threshold, and the absence of a mood disorder rules out schizoaffective disorder (F25) or mood-related psychosis. The prominent hallucinations and social/occupational decline argue against delusional disorder (F22) and unspecified psychosis (F28).
